references.text: 5. Moses repeats the prohibition against sowing two kinds of seed in a vineyard, plowing with an ox and a donkey together, and wearing clothing made of wool and linen mixed together. This expands on the laws concerning כִּלְאַיִם (mixed kinds) from 3. Moses.
The context for keeping the Lord's statutes (חֻקֹּת) and laws. The verse introduces the theme of obedience to God's commands, which also opens 19:19.
Concludes the chapter with a reminder to keep all the Lord's statutes (חֻקֹּתַי), which form the framework around the command in verse 19.
Repeats the command to keep all the Lord's statutes (חֻקֹּתַי) and laws, using the same wording as in 19:19.
Prohibits women from wearing men's clothing and vice versa, expanding on the theme of unnatural mixtures and the maintenance of God's created order.
The creation account shows that God created plants and animals 'according to their kind' (לְמִינֵהוּ). The prohibition against mixtures in 3. Moses 19:19 reflects this created order.
God created the animals 'according to their kind', serving as a theological basis for the prohibition against mating different animal species.
